# 1 Enoch Chapter 98 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Ge'ez MS; cf. 4QEn (Aramaic) | **Section:** Epistle of Enoch — Woe Oracles

---

**1** I am swearing this to you — wise and foolish alike: you will see many things in this world.

**2** Men will drape themselves in more jewels than women, in more elaborate clothing than young brides — all royalty and grandeur and power, drowning in silver and gold and purple, drowning in luxury and feasting.

**3** And for all of that, they will be empty of wisdom and understanding — and they will perish along with everything they accumulated. All that glory, all that splendor — and they end in shame, slaughter, and utter destitution. Their spirits will be hurled into the furnace of fire.

**4** I swear this to you, sinners: a mountain was never made into a slave. A hill was never made into someone's handmaid. In the same way, sin was never sent into the world as part of creation. Human beings invented it themselves. And those who commit it will fall under a terrible curse.

**5** Barrenness was not placed in women by God — it comes from the consequences of their own actions.

**6** I swear to you, sinners, by the Holy and Great One: every evil deed you have done is laid bare in heaven. Not one act of oppression is hidden. Not one is covered over.

**7** Don't tell yourself you don't know this. Don't convince yourself you don't see it. Every single sin is recorded in heaven every day, in the direct presence of the Most High.

**8** From this point on: understand that every act of oppression you commit is being written down — every day — until the day comes when you are judged.

**9** Woe to you, fools — you will be destroyed by your own foolishness. You attack the wise, and then wonder why good fortune never comes to you.

**10** Now hear this: you have already been prepared for the day of destruction. Stop hoping to live. You will leave, and you will die. There is no ransom that will buy your way out. You are set for the day of the great judgment — the day of tribulation and crushing shame for your spirits.

**11** Woe to you, hardhearted people who do evil and consume blood — where do you think all your food and drink comes from, all that abundance that fills you up? It all comes from the good things the Lord Most High spread across the earth in his generosity. And because of how you have used it, you will have no peace.

**12** Woe to you who have made unrighteousness your passion — why do you still expect things to go well for you? You will be handed over to the righteous, who will cut you down without mercy.

**13** Woe to you who cheer when righteous people suffer — no one will bury you.

**14** Woe to those who ignore the words of the righteous — you have no hope of life.

**15** Woe to those who fill scrolls with lies and godlessness — they write their lies so others will absorb them and be turned against their neighbors.

**16** Those people will find no peace. They will die fast.

---

*PNEUMA notes: V. 4 is the theological heart of this chapter — and one of the most important verses in all of 1 Enoch. Sin is not built into creation. God did not make the world broken. Human beings chose to create evil. This is the Enochic answer to theodicy: not dualism, but moral responsibility. V. 7's insistence that God records everything is the basis for the righteous hope: what is done in secret is known above.*
